b: one thing that kept slowing down our outreach was figuring out who the right person at each company actually was. we'd have a list of 60 or so companies, but then someone had to go through each website, figure out who handled marketing, find their contact details and check whether the email was valid. we'd also been paying for a yearly contact data plan, even though our lists weren't particularly large.

we recently tried handling that research through our agent with Monid. instead of immediately looking up emails, we start by checking the people associated with each company and filtering by role. it shows basic details first, so we can narrow things down before unlocking contact information. we tested it on 65 companies, and the whole run took under 10 minutes. the total came to around 3.80, including email verification. we're still reviewing the results, but the biggest difference has been spending less time manually sorting through contacts.
how do you usually decide who's worth reaching out to when you're building a list? do you research each company individually or have a process for narrowing down the right people?
